Verkhivka Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Verkhivka's original Jewish community was destroyed during the Haidamak Uprising before reviving in the 18th century; Rabbi Shmerl headed a local Hasidic community as early as the 1700s. During WWII, under Romanian Transnistria administration, several well-known families of the Vizhnitsky Hasidic dynasty — documented at length elsewhere in this collection — were transferred into Verkhivka's ghetto. When occupying authorities ordered the old wooden synagogue dismantled in November 1941, the community's shokhet managed to save its Torah scrolls. In December 1943, German forces began exterminating the ghetto's roughly 1,200 Jews, but for reasons that remain unclear, the effort was never completed, and some deported families returned after the war.
